navagio-beach.access: Boat only (Porto Vromi, Volimes, Zakynthos town). Swimming/landing rules have changed several times since 2018; check before booking.
navagio-beach.parking: Free lot at the clifftop viewpoint
navagio-beach.food: Cheap food stalls at the viewpoint lot (gyros etc.)
navagio-beach.note: Access rules (time limits, no swimming zones) changed in 2023; verify with port authority.

elafonissi-beach.access: Drive to lot, 5-10 min walk to sand
elafonissi-beach.sunbeds: Paid. Reported EUR 14-20 for 2 beds + umbrella (varies by source)
elafonissi-beach.food: Taverna near the parking lot, busy at lunch
elafonissi-beach.note: Sunbeds free up after ~14:00. Umbrellas sold at shops near the lot.

myrtos-beach.access: Steep road down, then pebble beach
myrtos-beach.parking: Free, large lot; fills in Jul-Aug (arrive before ~10:30)
myrtos-beach.sunbeds: Paid rental in organised section (price not found); some reports of free umbrellas
myrtos-beach.food: Canteen / small beach bar (usually from mid-June); delivery to umbrellas reported

balos-lagoon.access: Dirt road + walk from car park, or boat from Kissamos

sarakiniko.access: Short walk from car park; rocky, slippery
sarakiniko.sunbeds: None on the beach; deckchairs at nearby bar (price not confirmed)
sarakiniko.food: Food truck sometimes by the car park; not reliable
sarakiniko.note: Little shade; rock too hard for umbrellas. Bring water.

porto-katsiki.parking: Paid, about EUR 10/day car, EUR 3 motorbike (one review: EUR 5)
porto-katsiki.camper: Camper parking listed on campercontact.com (details not checked)
porto-katsiki.sunbeds: Limited; mostly reserved, price not found. Bring own
porto-katsiki.food: Canteens by the car park; restaurant above the beach delivers

voidokilia-beach.access: Dirt parking behind dunes, short walk
voidokilia-beach.food: No bar on beach; one source mentions a bar that delivers. Nearest food in Pylos
voidokilia-beach.note: Natura 2000 area beside Gialova Lagoon; bring all supplies.

egremni-beach.access: About 400 steps from top lot; sources conflict on whether the stairs are open
egremni-beach.food: Small restaurant and shop at top of stairs; cafe and toilets are up the steps

simos-beach.parking: Free, one large lot (full later in day)
simos-beach.camper: Simos Camping on site, about EUR 25-29/night (listing)
simos-beach.sunbeds: Paid, reported EUR 20-50 per set depending on type and year
simos-beach.food: Beach bars on site (names not confirmed)
simos-beach.note: Sunbed price varies widely by report. No shade without rental.

spiaggia-grande.access: Stairs from town (Via dei Mulini), SITA bus, or ferry to the pier
spiaggia-grande.parking: Hard to find; paid in town, from about EUR 10/hour with a 3-hour minimum (one review). Driving not advised
spiaggia-grande.sunbeds: Paid at private clubs: roughly EUR 20-35 pp budget, about EUR 30-50 per bed in reviews, premium clubs EUR 200+. Small free public section at the west end
spiaggia-grande.food: Restaurants and bars along Via Marina Grande and the promenade; some clubs serve food on the sand (e.g. Bruno, La Cambusa)
spiaggia-grande.note: Book clubs early in summer. Prices are indicative (blogs/reviews, some from 2024).

cala-goloritze.access: 3.5 km hike from Golgo plateau; booking required in season (cap 250/day)
cala-goloritze.parking: Su Porteddu hiker lot; ticket reportedly includes parking (one review: free lot, fills in August)
cala-goloritze.food: None on the beach. Bar at the trailhead is the last stop
cala-goloritze.note: Ticket EUR 7 pp via Heart of Sardinia app/site, bookable ~72 h ahead. Off-season no booking but fee at trailhead. Bring 2 L water.

la-pelosa.access: Walk from lot. Daily cap (1,500 in 2025 season 15 May-15 Oct), booking on official site
la-pelosa.parking: Paid, about EUR 2-3/hour, charged 08:00-20:00 (reports differ); fills by midday
la-pelosa.camper: Camper area listed on campercontact.com ('Area La Pelosa'); details not checked
la-pelosa.sunbeds: None on La Pelosa; neighbouring Gabbiano and La Pelosetta have rentable sunbeds. A beach mat is required
la-pelosa.toilets: Toilets/showers included in ticket (extra coin charge reported)
la-pelosa.note: 2025 ticket EUR 3.50 pp/day, under 12 free. 2026 rules not confirmed.

cala-mariolu.access: Boat (Cala Gonone, Santa Maria Navarrese, Arbatax; 40-60 min) or hard hike from Golgo (about 3 h)
cala-mariolu.parking: Free parking reported at Santa Maria Navarrese marina/town; Golgo trailhead not confirmed
cala-mariolu.note: Pebble beach, no natural shade. Busy Jul-Aug; go early or late.

scala-dei-turchi.parking: Day lot on SP68, EUR 6/day (Apr-Oct, 6 places, one listing); other lots nearby
scala-dei-turchi.camper: Paid camper area right at the entrance: about EUR 15-35/night depending on season, 27 spaces, 4 m height limit; services, showers, bar-restaurant, 220V
scala-dei-turchi.food: Bar-restaurant at camper area; restaurants and pizzerias nearby
scala-dei-turchi.toilets: Toilets and showers at the camper area
scala-dei-turchi.note: Camper area runs a tuk-tuk to beaches/lidos on request (cost not confirmed).

spiaggia-dei-conigli.access: Short path from road, or boat. Limited access

cala-violina.access: About 15-min walk from car park, or foot/bike/horse paths
cala-violina.parking: Paid; EUR 10 car + EUR 1 pp reported, booking online (limited places)
cala-violina.food: Small bar on the beach reported, plus a bar at the car park (drinks, pizza, sandwiches); one review says no food on beach
cala-violina.note: Reviews and fee are dated; check booking page. No shuttle found.

cala-luna.access: Boat from Cala Gonone (about 30 min, EUR 20-35 return) or demanding 3-5 h hike
cala-luna.sunbeds: Reported: sunbeds/umbrellas for rent near beach (sources differ); kayak/umbrella stand
cala-luna.food: Bar serving food and drinks on the beach
cala-luna.note: Boat extras: EUR 2 ecological + EUR 2 landing tax, cash.

cala-brandinchi.access: Walk from lot. Protected beach: booking mandatory in peak season (cap 1,500/day)

praia-da-marinha.access: Staircases down the cliff; no step-free access
praia-da-marinha.parking: Free cliff-top lot (about 32 spaces, paved); fills soon after sunrise, then police close the access road ~1 km out. Taxi/Uber may still reach the lot
praia-da-marinha.sunbeds: Not available (sources conflict; bring own shade)
praia-da-marinha.food: Snack bar on the beach (cash only reported); vans and stalls at cliff top
praia-da-marinha.toilets: Toilets at cliff-top lot; no showers
praia-da-marinha.note: Go at sunrise or late afternoon.

benagil-cove.access: Beach in village; cave only by kayak/SUP (about EUR 30/h) or boat
benagil-cove.parking: Scarce; firefighters' lot at top of hill about EUR 3 (tour operator listing)
benagil-cove.sunbeds: No sunbed rental; bring own parasol
benagil-cove.food: Snack shop on the beach; village restaurants close by
benagil-cove.note: Motorboat trips EUR 20-35 cruise past without landing. Summer boat slots sell out days ahead.

praia-dona-ana.parking: Paid parking nearby about EUR 2-4 for a few hours (~60 spaces), fills in summer; free farther away
praia-dona-ana.sunbeds: Paid: about EUR 10 per pair + parasol half day (2024 guide); EUR 20 full day reported. Limited
praia-dona-ana.food: Beach bar concession (beer, snacks). Better meals up in Lagos

praia-da-falesia.access: Long beach with several clifftop access points; stairs down to the sand
praia-da-falesia.parking: Clifftop car parks, reported free but limited; they fill by afternoon in peak season
praia-da-falesia.sunbeds: Sunbed hire at the main access points
praia-da-falesia.food: Restaurants and beach bars along the beach
praia-da-falesia.toilets: Toilets reported along the beach; some sources say paid
praia-da-falesia.lifeguard: Supervised sections only (e.g. Olhos de Agua, Acoteias); season reported as roughly June-September
praia-da-falesia.note: Reported Blue Flag beach. Confirm lifeguard dates and current facilities locally.

praia-do-camilo.access: About 200 wooden steps; not for limited mobility
praia-do-camilo.parking: Small cliff-top lot, limited; some say free early morning. Chaos by ~10:00 in summer
praia-do-camilo.food: Snack bar at bottom of stairs (one review); cafe O Camilo at the top
praia-do-camilo.note: Open status of the beach bar varies by season.

praia-de-odeceixe.parking: Described as straightforward; fee not found
praia-de-odeceixe.camper: Day parking 08:00-20:00 reported, overnight stays prohibited; motorhomes reported barred from the village (signs before the bridge); municipal camper area 3 km away with free services
praia-de-odeceixe.sunbeds: Sunbeds mentioned in one guide (price not found); kayak, SUP, surfboard rentals
praia-de-odeceixe.food: Four commercial establishments on beach, from cafe to restaurant
praia-de-odeceixe.note: Camper rules conflict; confirm with Camara de Aljezur.

praia-da-ursa.access: About 2.6 km round trip from Cabo da Roca; last 400 m steep cliff descent, no stairs
praia-da-ursa.parking: Small lot on the cliff reached by dirt road off the Cabo da Roca road
praia-da-ursa.note: Not advised in rain or wind. Bring water and food.

praia-do-carvalho.access: Tunnel cut in the rock, steep uneven steps; not suitable for wheelchairs
praia-do-carvalho.parking: Cliff-top near tunnel entrance (details not found)
praia-do-carvalho.food: Sources conflict: no facilities vs. a small cliff bar; bring own food and drink
praia-do-carvalho.note: Part of the sand is in a landslide-risk zone (limited-use beach).

praia-da-adraga.access: Road to small cliff-side valley beach
praia-da-adraga.parking: Small lot (~50 cars), about EUR 3/day reported; overflow up the valley. Restaurant parking free if early
praia-da-adraga.food: Adraga restaurant on the beach (seafood; book ahead for dinner); Bar do Fundo nearby
praia-da-adraga.note: Strong surf and currents. No public transport.

es-trenc.access: Several access points; 1.5 km walk from Sa Barralina lot; shuttle has run

cala-macarelleta.access: Reached on foot from Cala Macarella next door; summer bus-only from Ciutadella (June-Sept, about EUR 8.40 return, in 2023; check current)
cala-macarelleta.parking: Sources conflict: one paid and one free lot, free lot with campers overnight; car access banned May-Sept in some years
cala-macarelleta.food: No restaurant at Macarelleta. Susy's Chiringuito on Macarella (meat, fish, salads)
cala-macarelleta.note: Rules are 2018-2024 data; confirm with Consell de Menorca.

ses-illetes.access: Inside Ses Salines natural park; scooter/bike/car
ses-illetes.parking: Parking near La Savina; park access toll EUR 5 reported by one Aug 2025 visitor (unit unclear)
ses-illetes.food: Very expensive per reviews: Juan y Andrea restaurant; EUR 7 water, EUR 50 pasta, EUR 27 sandwich reported at beach bars
ses-illetes.note: Scooter rental about EUR 15-20/day low season, EUR 30-45 high. Taxi back to Pujols about EUR 18.

as-catedrais.access: Staircase; tide-dependent; free permit needed Easter week and 1 Jul-30 Sep (book on Xunta site)
as-catedrais.parking: Two large free lots (paved + gravel); hard to find a space in summer
as-catedrais.note: Visit around low tide (arrive about 2 h before). Dogs restricted Easter and 15 May-15 Sep.

cala-mondrago.access: 10 min walk from lot (Mallorca natural park)
cala-mondrago.parking: Paid, about EUR 5-6 per car, reduced after 17:00 (EUR 3); about 300 spaces, many shaded
cala-mondrago.sunbeds: Limited sunbeds and parasols, price not found
cala-mondrago.food: Beach bar with drinks and light food (lease uncertain as of 2018)
cala-mondrago.note: Pay parking in cash. Bar status may have changed since 2018.

cala-varques.access: 15-60 min walk; stony path, sturdy shoes
cala-varques.parking: No official lot. Old Ma-4014 section closed with bollards (Mar 2026); roadside parking prohibited, fines reported
cala-varques.food: None (makeshift bar mentioned once); bring water
cala-varques.note: Manacor council limiting access amid congestion (Mar 2026). Check before driving.

cala-de-la-granadella.access: Shuttle/train from upper lot or walk
cala-de-la-granadella.parking: Guardia Park lot about 200 spaces, barriers in Jul-Aug; fee not confirmed. Shuttle about EUR 5 pp (11:00-20:00, not running in 2022)
cala-de-la-granadella.sunbeds: Rented via concession (low cost; price not found); hammocks too
cala-de-la-granadella.food: Three restaurants at the cove per Javea tourism (names not confirmed)
cala-de-la-granadella.note: Pebble beach: bring water shoes. Arrive before 10:00 peak season.

praia-de-rodas.access: Ferry from Vigo (40-50 min), Cangas or Baiona; free Xunta permit (cap 2,200/day) obtained before ferry ticket
praia-de-rodas.camper: Camping only: official Cies campsite near Rodas; reservations open 1 March; overnight allowed Easter week and 15 May-15 Sep
praia-de-rodas.food: Restaurant next to the pier on Rodas; on-site restaurant at campsite
praia-de-rodas.note: Ferry ticket needs permit code. Exchange digital ticket for paper before boarding.

cala-pregonda.access: 20-35 min walk from Binimel-la lot, no shade
cala-pregonda.parking: Free lot at Binimel-la (150+ spaces), fills before ~10:00
cala-pregonda.food: No bar on beach; a bar/restaurant at end of car park
cala-pregonda.toilets: None on beach; nearest at Binimel-la
cala-pregonda.note: Parking is free per older sources; not re-checked.

zlatni-rat.access: Free beach access; 20-25 min walk from Bol town through pine woods, or taxi
zlatni-rat.parking: Paid; EUR 10-25/day depending on source (2026 reviews EUR 10-20). Cheaper lots a few hundred metres away
zlatni-rat.sunbeds: Paid, EUR 10-15 per sunbed (2026), umbrella extra; EUR 13 each reported; set-back bed EUR 44
zlatni-rat.food: Restaurants and cafes in the area (menus not checked)
zlatni-rat.note: Beach access itself is free. Taxi stand in Bol centre; taxi boat from port about EUR 4.

sakarun-beach.access: Road to beach; tourist train from Bozava (4 km) in summer
sakarun-beach.parking: Paid in season: EUR 6 for 2 h (recent review), free off-season; some park on roadside
sakarun-beach.sunbeds: Loungers and umbrellas for rent (price not found)
sakarun-beach.food: Two catering facilities (beach bars, a burger place), serve in high season
sakarun-beach.toilets: One chemical toilet reported (for bar users)
sakarun-beach.note: No campsite at Sakarun itself; campsites near Veli Rat (separate beach).

stiniva.access: Steep 30-45 min hike, or by boat from Vis Town / Komiza; tour boats arrive 10:00-16:00
stiniva.parking: Conflicting: no dedicated parking vs. lot at top of hill
stiniva.food: Sources conflict: small bar at the bottom vs. no cafes or toilets. Bring water and food
stiniva.note: Go early; avoid midday tour boats. Not accessible for disabled visitors.

punta-rata.parking: Prices inconsistent: from EUR 4/h up to EUR 25/day (reviews)
punta-rata.sunbeds: Paid; reports EUR 28 for 2 loungers + parasol, or EUR 7 bed + EUR 5 umbrella (old)
punta-rata.food: Restaurants and cafes nearby; terrace Adriatik recommended by one visitor
punta-rata.note: Very crowded in August. Reviews dated; no official price list found.

banje-beach.access: Public beach by Dubrovnik Old Town (Ploce)

dubovica.access: Steep 10-15 min path; not accessible for mobility impairments
dubovica.parking: Free roadside verge, very limited; fills by 09:00 in Jul-Aug
dubovica.sunbeds: Sources conflict: none vs. EUR 15-20 per pair at the bar (one source)
dubovica.food: Konoba Dubovica (fried fish, shrimp) and Duba Beach Bar (cocktails; reportedly no beer/food, one review)
dubovica.note: About 8 km from Hvar Town. Bring shoes, shade, water.

saplunara.access: Road on Mljet, about 16 km from Sobra ferry port; taxi safer than bus
saplunara.parking: About EUR 5/day, limited in peak summer
saplunara.food: Beach bars June-Sept (Hippocampus, Al Panchetto, Mala Saplunara, Kod Ante named in one listing)
saplunara.toilets: Toilet and shower listed in one source
saplunara.note: One visitor complained of dirt and yachts. No direct ferry.

rajska-plaza.parking: Car park nearby, about 200 spaces (fee not found)
rajska-plaza.camper: Camping San Marino beside the beach: pitches from about EUR 40/night (EUR 40-90 range)
rajska-plaza.sunbeds: Loungers and parasols for rent (price not found)
rajska-plaza.food: Several beach bars: Sunset, Bamboocho, Trstika, Pocco Locco, Porto, Spot Bar

bacvice.food: Cafes and restaurants in the pavilion behind the beach; party area at night

sunj-beach.access: Ferry from Dubrovnik (Gruz) to Lopud harbour, then 20-45 min walk or EUR 3 golf-buggy
sunj-beach.sunbeds: Paid via bars: about EUR 10 per bed full day (reviews)
sunj-beach.food: Beach bars along the back of the beach (party spot); bring own water to save
sunj-beach.toilets: Public toilet at Beach Bar Sunj; open shower EUR 1
sunj-beach.note: Ferry fare about EUR 10 (old listing); check Jadrolinija.

palombaggia.parking: Free lot at NE end fills fast; paid lots reported EUR 4-15/day, one at EUR 35 (meter, to 14:30). Prices differ by lot
palombaggia.sunbeds: Rentable but limited; no reliable price. Palm Beach club sunbeds criticised as overpriced
palombaggia.food: Several beach restaurants (Palm Beach: seafood/Med); bring cash. Example: 2 coffees EUR 5, 2 ice creams EUR 10
palombaggia.note: Reviews only; no official tariff found.

saleccia.access: Taxi boat from Saint-Florent (about 20-45 min, EUR 25-30 return), 4x4 track 12 km from Casta (about 1 h + 10-15 min walk), or 4-5 h hike
saleccia.parking: Paid EUR 5-10 near the beach (sources differ)
saleccia.food: One snack bar / simple restaurant reported; bring picnic
saleccia.note: Boat + 4x4 package from about EUR 55. Camping U Paradisu nearby.

santa-giulia.food: Bars and restaurants along the shore (about 5 beach restaurants per one listing)

rondinara-beach.access: Road to the back of the bay
rondinara-beach.parking: About EUR 5-6/day (2020 / 2025 sources); may be free out of season
rondinara-beach.camper: Camping Rondinara next to the beach: about EUR 29/night without electricity; open about 15 May-30 Sep (2025); beach parking reportedly included for campers
rondinara-beach.food: Chez Ange restaurant near the parking; campsite has snack bar, pizzeria, restaurant
rondinara-beach.note: Narrow bendy road. Pay by card or cash unclear.

pampelonne-beach.access: Six access points along a 5 km beach
pampelonne-beach.parking: Paid, about EUR 4-5/day; hard in Jul-Aug; some clubs offer valet
pampelonne-beach.camper: Paid motorhome area behind the beach: EUR 22/night from 1 April 2026 (single night tickets), no electricity/toilets/showers; bridge limit 5.5 t
pampelonne-beach.sunbeds: Paid and varied: about EUR 30-60 per person per day, up to EUR 100; Shellona EUR 300-500+ (includes lunch). Free public sand sections
pampelonne-beach.food: Beach clubs: Club 55 (expensive), L'Esquinade (cheaper). Book ahead in Jul-Aug
pampelonne-beach.toilets: Public toilets and showers near access points
pampelonne-beach.note: Part of the beach is naturist.

en-vau-calanque.access: Hike from Cassis (7.8 km, 3 h, 360 m climb; final descent steep) or about 60-90 min from Port-Miou / D559 parking
en-vau-calanque.parking: Paid meter parking in Cassis; Col de la Gardiole lot no longer available; Port-Miou hard on weekends
en-vau-calanque.food: None; bring all water and food (1.5 L min.)
en-vau-calanque.note: Access rules change yearly with fire risk. Check Calanques National Park site / Mes Calanques app.

plage-notre-dame.access: Ferry from Tour Fondue (15 min) or La Londe (free parking at Port Miramar), then 3.5 km by bike (25 min) or walk (45 min)
plage-notre-dame.parking: No cars on Porquerolles; bike parking at beach
plage-notre-dame.sunbeds: Unconfirmed; one 2016 blog says no sunbeds/umbrellas on island beaches
plage-notre-dame.food: No restaurant at Notre-Dame; restaurant and sunbed hire at Plage d'Argent
plage-notre-dame.lifeguard: Only Plage d'Argent has a lifeguard
plage-notre-dame.note: Free access. Rent bikes ahead in high season.

calanque-de-sormiou.access: Road closed to cars for non-residents from first April weekend to All Saints, except restaurant customers; or walk about 1 h from Cayolle lot
calanque-de-sormiou.parking: Outer Cayolle lot about EUR 4.5-5, unsupervised; inner lot for restaurant customers (reserve at Le Chateau)
calanque-de-sormiou.food: Restaurant Le Chateau (reservation also gives parking access)
calanque-de-sormiou.note: Park limits visitors in peak: free online reservation (3 days ahead). Can close for fire risk.

blue-lagoon-comino.access: Ferry from Cirkewwa or Mgarr, or cruise; free Natura 2000 pass required to land (limited daily)
blue-lagoon-comino.sunbeds: Paid, about EUR 15-20 per set/person; limited by midday
blue-lagoon-comino.food: Food trucks; prices high (juice EUR 8, pizza/burger EUR 10)
blue-lagoon-comino.note: Ferry about EUR 10-15 return; cruises EUR 13-45. Go before 09:15 or after 17:00.

golden-bay.parking: Two lots: one free smaller lot reported, other about EUR 1/h; full by 09:00 in summer
golden-bay.sunbeds: Paid, about EUR 17 for 2 loungers + umbrella; lockers EUR 5
golden-bay.food: Several beach restaurants, snack bars; lunch about EUR 20

ghajn-tuffieha-bay.parking: Top lot: free but full after 09:30 (one source) or about EUR 1.50/h
ghajn-tuffieha-bay.sunbeds: For hire (Riviera Martinique Lido); price not found
ghajn-tuffieha-bay.food: Snack bar / kiosk at corner of bay (overpriced per one guide)

ramla-bay.parking: Free along the access road; private lot EUR 2/day
ramla-bay.sunbeds: Paid: about EUR 15 for 2 loungers + parasol (2021), EUR 5-7 per item
ramla-bay.food: Snack kiosks and two basic beach restaurants

ghadira-bay.parking: Free car parks along the beach; fill by 09:00 in summer
ghadira-bay.sunbeds: Paid, about EUR 12-20 per set (2 beds + umbrella)
ghadira-bay.food: About 9 restaurants and bars (Sol Beach Bar, Munchies, Maxima Lido, Ventuno, San Remo) plus kiosks
ghadira-bay.toilets: Toilet access often included with rental

st-peter-s-pool.access: Rocky inlet with ladders; walk from lot
st-peter-s-pool.parking: First lot about EUR 3 (cash), or free dirt lot further down; full by 09:00 in Jul-Aug
st-peter-s-pool.food: No bar; one cash snack van in summer (not reliable)

san-blas-bay.access: About 200 steps or rough track; do not drive down
san-blas-bay.parking: Small lot at top, very limited
san-blas-bay.sunbeds: Sources conflict: none vs. kiosk rentals
san-blas-bay.food: Small summer kiosk (drinks, snacks) per some sources
san-blas-bay.note: Summer jeep shuttle about EUR 2.50 pp; bus 303 then 600-650 m walk.

sveti-stefan.access: Public beach north of island; island itself private (entry EUR 25 pp per one guide, under 12 free). Queen's Beach reserved for Aman guests
sveti-stefan.parking: Paid, about EUR 2-4/hour (flat EUR 12 older); usually packed. Some free spots before entrance
sveti-stefan.sunbeds: Paid: EUR 30-60 per set; first row EUR 77, second EUR 66 (2024); south side about EUR 100/day. Free public section to lay a towel
sveti-stefan.food: Restaurants on island (table booking); cafes nearby

jaz-beach.parking: Large lot reported free with spaces even in the afternoon; campervans can park
jaz-beach.camper: Camping Jaz at the beach (rates not found; sanitary blocks reported in poor shape)
jaz-beach.sunbeds: Paid, about EUR 10 for 2 sunbeds + umbrella (reviews); some areas free
jaz-beach.food: Shops, restaurants and numerous bars near camp; supermarket on site
jaz-beach.note: Part of the beach is naturist. Concert venue in some summers.

valdanos-bay.access: 10 min drive from Ulcinj; narrow road through olive grove; taxi EUR 5-7
valdanos-bay.parking: Large free outdoor lot, partly shaded
valdanos-bay.sunbeds: Sunbeds for hire (price not found); room for own umbrella
valdanos-bay.food: Beach bar (pizza, drinks) and on-site restaurant
valdanos-bay.note: Pebbles: water shoes. Upkeep inconsistent (litter reported).

kamenovo.access: 5 min walk from Rafailovici; steep cliff path from parking
kamenovo.parking: Reports conflict: free vs paid EUR 3-5/day (card accepted)
kamenovo.sunbeds: Paid: EUR 15-25 per bed by row, EUR 20-30 per set; bring own umbrella and towel to use beach free
kamenovo.food: Two restaurants (one with beach service), bars; small beer EUR 2.90-4.60

ksamil-beaches.access: Several small beaches; some via unpaved roads
ksamil-beaches.parking: Pulebardha lot EUR 1; free lots elsewhere (Edon-Bina free, 10 min walk). Hard to find parking near popular bays by 10:00
ksamil-beaches.sunbeds: Paid: EUR 10-30 per 2 beds + umbrella, up to EUR 40+ peak; Beach 1 800-1,500 ALL, Beach 2 500-1,000, Beach 3 500-800. Fee often waived with food/drink
ksamil-beaches.food: Beach restaurants and bars at most rented sections
ksamil-beaches.note: Very few free spots in high season; Beach 3 has the most free sand.

gjipe.access: 30-45 min walk (2.5 km) from parking, or boat from Himara / water taxi EUR 15-20; jeep rides in summer 500-1,000 ALL; canyon route is hard
gjipe.parking: Paid: 200 lek pp or 300 lek/day (EUR 3), 1,000 lek overnight
gjipe.camper: Camping allowed; Gjipe Eco Campground (flush toilets, cold showers, restaurant, bar, SUP/canoe rental); day tickets sold for showers/toilets

praia-do-seixal.note: Dark volcanic sand under green cliffs on the north coast of Madeira. The Atlantic can be rough.

ilha-de-tavira.access: Moderate: short ferry or boat from Tavira, then a walk on the island
ilha-de-tavira.parking: On the mainland near the ferry; check locally
ilha-de-tavira.food: Cafes and restaurants near the ferry landing; check locally
ilha-de-tavira.note: Long barrier island with calm lagoon water and open Atlantic beach. Check last ferry time.

playa-de-cabopino.access: Easy: flat access from the marina and car park
playa-de-cabopino.parking: Car park near the marina; check locally
playa-de-cabopino.food: Beach bars and restaurants near the marina; check locally
playa-de-cabopino.note: Sandy beach beside a marina and old watchtower, backed by dunes and pines. Part of the beach is used by naturists.

playa-de-zahara-de-los-atunes.access: Easy: flat access from the village and access points
playa-de-zahara-de-los-atunes.parking: Parking near the village and beach access points; check locally
playa-de-zahara-de-los-atunes.food: Beach bars and restaurants in the village; check locally
playa-de-zahara-de-los-atunes.note: Wide Atlantic beach of fine sand. Wind and surf can be strong.

maspalomas-dunes.access: Moderate: walk across soft sand dunes from the access points
maspalomas-dunes.parking: Car parks near the lighthouse and beach access; check locally
maspalomas-dunes.sunbeds: Available on the beach side; check locally
maspalomas-dunes.food: Kiosks and beach bars along the beach edge; check locally
maspalomas-dunes.note: Protected dune field meeting the Atlantic. Bring water and shade. Stay on marked routes. Parts of the beach are used by naturists.

playa-de-las-canteras.access: Easy: flat promenade the whole length of the beach
playa-de-las-canteras.parking: Paid car parks nearby; check locally
playa-de-las-canteras.food: Cafes and restaurants along the promenade
playa-de-las-canteras.note: Long city beach sheltered by a natural reef. Check flags and tide levels.

el-cotillo-beach.access: Easy: short walk from the village and parking areas
el-cotillo-beach.parking: Parking near the village and beach access points; check locally
el-cotillo-beach.food: Cafes and restaurants in El Cotillo village; check locally
el-cotillo-beach.note: Wide sandy beach with steady wind and windsurfers. Some sections have rocks in the water.

praia-de-burgau.access: Easy: short walk from the village
praia-de-burgau.parking: Street parking in the village and a car park nearby; check locally
praia-de-burgau.food: Cafes and restaurants in the village; check locally
praia-de-burgau.note: Small sandy beach below a whitewashed village. Can be busy in July and August.

playa-de-la-barrosa.access: Easy. Flat promenade and ramps down to the sand along most of the beach.
playa-de-la-barrosa.parking: Free and paid car parks along the promenade; the central ones fill by midday in July and August.
playa-de-la-barrosa.sunbeds: Sunbed and umbrella rental on the central stretch near the main chiringuitos; the north end is mostly free sand.
playa-de-la-barrosa.food: Several chiringuitos serving fried fish, grilled sardines and cold drinks; more restaurants behind the promenade.
playa-de-la-barrosa.note: The tide is wide: at low tide the sand flats and rock pools stretch far out. Lifeguards in summer. Levante wind can be strong.

praia-do-castelejo.access: Moderate. Short walk down a dirt path from the car park to the sand.
praia-do-castelejo.parking: Free dirt car park above the beach; space is limited in July and August.
praia-do-castelejo.sunbeds: None. Bring your own umbrella, though the wind can be strong.
praia-do-castelejo.food: Small seasonal beach bar; otherwise bring water and snacks, or drive to Vila do Bispo.
praia-do-castelejo.note: Atlantic swell, strong currents and cold water. Seasonal lifeguard only. Popular with surfers; check conditions before swimming.

arromanches-gold-beach.access: Easy. Flat seafront promenade with direct access to the sand.
arromanches-gold-beach.parking: Paid car parks in town, a few minutes on foot from the beach.
arromanches-gold-beach.sunbeds: No sunbed rental; this is an open, public beach.
arromanches-gold-beach.food: Cafes, creperies and restaurants along the seafront and in the town centre.
arromanches-gold-beach.note: Tides here are large and the sea returns quickly across the flats; check tide times before walking out toward the Mulberry harbour remains. Lifeguard in July and August.

is-arutas.access: Easy. The car park is close to the sand.
is-arutas.parking: Paid car park close to the beach; it fills early in summer, and rates vary by season.
is-arutas.sunbeds: Sunbed and umbrella rental in season; you can also bring your own umbrella.
is-arutas.food: Beach bar and seafood restaurants nearby in season.
is-arutas.note: The coarse quartz sand is protected, so do not take any home. Arrive early in July and August to find space.

praia-do-barril.access: Moderate. A flat, hard path of about 1.3 km from Santa Luzia, on foot (around 15 minutes) or by the small tourist train; the path suits pushchairs.
praia-do-barril.parking: Paid car park near the start of the path in Santa Luzia; check the time limit before you leave the car.
praia-do-barril.sunbeds: Check on arrival; rental is not guaranteed outside the summer season.
praia-do-barril.food: Beach bars and restaurants in season; more choice in Santa Luzia, known for octopus dishes.
praia-do-barril.note: The anchor memorial in the dunes is a short walk behind the beach. The beach is large, so there is space even in summer.

playa-de-calahonda.access: Moderate. Reached through the Boquete de Calahonda arch behind the Balcon de Europa, then a zigzag of steps; not suitable for pushchairs or limited mobility.
playa-de-calahonda.parking: No parking at the beach; use the town car parks and walk to the Balcon de Europa.
playa-de-calahonda.sunbeds: Sunbed rental, showers and toilets in high season.
playa-de-calahonda.food: Cafes and restaurants along the Balcon de Europa above the beach; a snack stand has been reported on the sand.
playa-de-calahonda.note: Lifeguard and sunbeds run mainly in high season, and beach businesses have changed over the years, so check on arrival.

plakias-beach.access: Easy. Flat access from the village seafront.
plakias-beach.parking: Parking in and around the village; plenty of space outside peak season.
plakias-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas by stretch; prices vary, so compare before you sit. Some beach bars lend umbrellas to customers.
plakias-beach.food: Many tavernas and beach bars along the waterfront, and supermarkets in the village.
plakias-beach.note: Strong wind makes the beach hard to use, so check the forecast. Part of the beach near a large rock is used by naturists.

paleokastritsa-beach.access: Moderate. Steep steps lead to some of the coves; the main beach is the easiest.
paleokastritsa-beach.parking: Paid car park behind the main beach; it fills early in July and August.
paleokastritsa-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas rented at the main beach, with showers and changing rooms.
paleokastritsa-beach.food: Tavernas around the beaches and the harbour.
paleokastritsa-beach.note: Tour coaches arrive from about 11am to 3pm in high season, so go early or late. Boat trips to sea caves and quiet coves leave from the harbour and can sell out in summer.

cala-rossa.access: Moderate. A long staircase leads down to the rocky bay; not suitable for wheelchairs.
cala-rossa.parking: No dedicated car park at the cove; street parking near the entrance, or come by bike.
cala-rossa.sunbeds: No sunbed rental reported; bring your own shade.
cala-rossa.food: No food reported at the cove; bring water and snacks.
cala-rossa.note: Rocky shore with no sand, so water shoes help. Sources disagree on how easy swimming is, so take care on the rocks.

playa-de-zarautz.access: Easy. Flat promenade along the whole beach.
playa-de-zarautz.parking: Parking in town, within about ten minutes on foot of the sand.
playa-de-zarautz.food: Bars and restaurants along the promenade.
playa-de-zarautz.note: About 2.5 km long and 80 m wide, with several surf schools. Lifeguard cover is listed from 10am to 8pm in season.

cala-tarida.access: Easy. A road leads down to the beach car park.
cala-tarida.parking: Small car park; the narrow access road backs up by early afternoon in peak summer, so park early.
cala-tarida.sunbeds: Sunbed and parasol hire from beach bars; prices vary, so check on arrival.
cala-tarida.food: Beach bars, beach clubs and restaurants on and above the beach.
cala-tarida.note: West-facing, so it is a good sunset spot. Summer bus services run from Ibiza Town and Sant Antoni.

praia-de-carcavelos.parking: Free and paid parking nearby; lots fill fast in summer, so arrive early or take the train.
praia-de-carcavelos.sunbeds: Check on arrival; rental is not confirmed.
praia-de-carcavelos.food: Cafes and restaurants along the promenade.
praia-de-carcavelos.note: Surf schools and lifeguards in season; swimming areas are separated from surfing zones in summer. The train from Cais do Sodre takes about 26 minutes and the station is roughly 15 minutes on foot from the sand.

aiguablava-beach.access: Moderate. The cove lies below the Parador on the cliff; step details were not confirmed.
aiguablava-beach.parking: Car park next to the Parador, paid in summer.
aiguablava-beach.food: Summer beach restaurant (Mar i Vent) in the cove and the Parador restaurant above.
aiguablava-beach.note: Toilets and adapted showers, plus water sports and a diving centre. The cove is small and fills early in high season.

agiofili-beach.access: Moderate. About 2 km from Vasiliki by a road that mostly climbs; boat taxis also run from the village, and walking is possible but hot.
agiofili-beach.parking: Paid car park just before the beach gate; rates vary by season (roughly 8 to 10 euros reported).
agiofili-beach.sunbeds: Reports differ: some guides list sunbed and parasol rental (around 20 euros), others say organised sunbeds are gone; bring your own shade to be safe.
agiofili-beach.food: A kiosk near the car park; no taverna close by, so bring food.
agiofili-beach.note: Toilet and shower block near the parking area. Gate hours are reported inconsistently, so check locally before you go.

kamari-beach.access: Easy. Flat seafront promenade with direct access to the sand.
kamari-beach.parking: Several free car parks near the beach.
kamari-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas rented along most of the beach; arrive early for the day.
kamari-beach.food: Tavernas, snack bars and cafes along the seafront.
kamari-beach.note: The dark volcanic sand and pebbles get very hot at midday, so waterproof sandals help. Lifeguard cover is reported in summer.

kleftiko.access: Challenging. Reached only by boat; there is no road and no beach facilities.
kleftiko.parking: Not applicable; tours leave from Adamas port or Agia Kiriaki beach.
kleftiko.sunbeds: None; you swim and snorkel from the boat.
kleftiko.food: None on land; boat tours typically provide water and snacks, and some include lunch.
kleftiko.note: Half-day tours usually allow about one to one and a half hours at Kleftiko. Routes can change in strong north winds.

praia-de-monte-gordo.access: Easy. Flat promenade and wide sand with a gentle slope into the sea.
praia-de-monte-gordo.parking: Free and paid parking nearby, including street parking; busy at peak times.
praia-de-monte-gordo.sunbeds: Sunbed rental available; reported at about 15 to 20 euros for two loungers and an umbrella.
praia-de-monte-gordo.food: Restaurants and shops along the promenade.
praia-de-monte-gordo.note: Blue Flag beach with lifeguards in summer. Toilets and showers on the promenade, though one reviewer found public toilets hard to find.

ses-salines.access: Easy. Short walk from the car parks over flat ground.
ses-salines.parking: Small free lot by the road that fills early; larger paid car park near the roundabout.
ses-salines.sunbeds: Loungers and parasols available; beach clubs can be pricey.
ses-salines.food: Beach clubs, bars and restaurants along the sand.
ses-salines.note: Inside the Ses Salines natural park, with dunes and pine woods behind. Summer buses run from Ibiza Town; check current timetables.

paraggi-beach.access: Moderate. The coast path from Santa Margherita takes about 30 minutes; a bus also runs, and the nearest train station is in Santa Margherita, about 2.5 km away.
paraggi-beach.parking: Parking is scarce and expensive; arrive early if driving, or take the bus from Rapallo or Santa Margherita.
paraggi-beach.sunbeds: Paid lidos at either end of the bay; prices are very high (reports range from about 70 euros to over 200 euros for two beds and an umbrella), so check before you sit.
paraggi-beach.food: Cafes and restaurants at the lidos and along the bay.
paraggi-beach.note: A free public stretch lies in the middle of the beach; bring your own towel and umbrella to use it.

praia-do-baleal.access: Easy. Road access to the beach and the village.
praia-do-baleal.parking: Parking around Baleal bay and along the road, plus a car park by the cafe at nearby Supertubos.
praia-do-baleal.sunbeds: No sunbed rental reported; this is a surf beach, so bring your own shade.
praia-do-baleal.food: Beach bars and cafes in Baleal, with many surf shops.
praia-do-baleal.note: The north-facing side is about 800 m long and sheltered by a small island to the west. Many surf schools and camps operate here; check the swell before swimming.

itzurun-beach.access: Moderate. Flat tree-lined promenade from the town centre, but access onto the sand and along the cliffs may be harder; step details were not confirmed.
itzurun-beach.parking: Free car park on the harbour side, about a 15-minute walk away; street parking near the beach is limited and many streets are one-way.
itzurun-beach.food: Cafes and shops in Zumaia town, a short walk from the sand.
itzurun-beach.note: The beach is about 270 m long with golden sand and heavy swell. Low tide reveals the rock formations, so check tide times.

cala-millor.access: Easy. Flat promenade with a cycle path and footpath along the beach.
cala-millor.parking: Parking near the promenade is available but limited in peak season.
cala-millor.food: Many restaurants and hotels along the palm-lined promenade.
cala-millor.note: Lifeguards are reported in peak season. Sources give the beach length as anywhere from about 1.3 km to 2 km; several describe it as Blue Flag, so check the current award.

monterosso-al-mare.access: Easy. A short walk from the train station to the beach.
monterosso-al-mare.parking: Reached on foot from the station, so a car is not needed.
monterosso-al-mare.sunbeds: Paid areas rent two sunbeds and a parasol (about 25 to 40 euros a day reported, often cash only); a small free area sits in front of the station exit.
monterosso-al-mare.food: Beachside cafes and bars at the lidos and in the village.
monterosso-al-mare.note: Bring water shoes for the pebbles at the water line. The area near the Giant statue is quieter and has shallow water for young children.

cala-sisine.access: Boat from Cala Gonone or Santa Maria Navarrese, or on foot: about 1 km from the Planu e Murta parking (4x4 road) or about 8 km from Ololbissi
cala-sisine.parking: No parking at the beach; park at Golgo-side areas or in Cala Gonone and take a boat
cala-sisine.food: Small seasonal bar near the beach
cala-sisine.note: Dirt roads can be difficult after rain. Check conditions locally. Boats from Cala Gonone are the easiest option.

sa-calobra.access: Mountain road from Sa Calobra car park, then short tunnels to the cove; boats also run from Port de Soller
sa-calobra.parking: Paid car park at the port; fills in summer; prices vary by source
sa-calobra.sunbeds: None found on the pebble beach
sa-calobra.food: Cafes and restaurants by the port
sa-calobra.note: Pebble beach at the mouth of the Torrent de Pareis gorge. Arrive early or late to avoid coaches.

kolymbithres-beach.access: Short walk from the road; bus or water taxi from Naoussa
kolymbithres-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas run by beach clubs; prices not found
kolymbithres-beach.food: Tavernas very close to the beach
kolymbithres-beach.note: Granite rock formations separate small coves. Water sports such as kayaks and SUP are available. Arrive early in summer.

playa-burriana.parking: Pay car park at the western end plus street parking; fills early in summer
playa-burriana.sunbeds: Sunbed and parasol hire along most of the beach; price not found
playa-burriana.food: Chiringuitos and restaurants along the beach
playa-burriana.note: About 800 m long and 40 m wide. Lifeguards and showers in season. Blue Flag status reported.

cala-agulla.access: Path through the pine forest from the car park area
cala-agulla.parking: Car park reported closed since February 2025; check current status
cala-agulla.sunbeds: Sunbed and umbrella rental available; price not found
cala-agulla.note: Bay roughly 500 to 800 m long and about 50 m deep. Parking status has been unclear, so check before you go.

mylopotas-beach.access: Easy; walk or bus from Chora (about 2 km)
mylopotas-beach.parking: No dedicated public parking found; bus every 15 to 20 minutes in peak season
mylopotas-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas available; price not found; book ahead in July and August
mylopotas-beach.food: Beach bars and tavernas along the bay, mostly at the southern end
mylopotas-beach.note: Horseshoe bay over 1 km of golden sand. Busiest beach on Ios; walk north for a quieter stretch.

canyamel-beach.access: Easy, flat access from the village
canyamel-beach.parking: No beach-specific parking details found; arrive early in summer
canyamel-beach.sunbeds: Sunbed and parasol hire available; price not found
canyamel-beach.note: About 290 to 350 m long depending on source. Toilets and showers available.

levanto-beach.access: Easy; short walk from the town and train station
levanto-beach.parking: Paid car parks in town; the lot above the beach has a reduced hourly rate; passes about 5 EUR/day via rentals
levanto-beach.sunbeds: Paid lidos along the beach; prices not found; free sections available
levanto-beach.food: Cafes and restaurants along the promenade
levanto-beach.note: Sand and pebbles. Surf school operates year-round. Cycle path along the old railway to Bonassola and Framura.

cala-galdana.access: Easy; flat access from the resort; bus stop nearby
cala-galdana.parking: Free car parks 5 to 15 minutes on foot, including Cala Mitjana; fills by midday
cala-galdana.sunbeds: Sunbed and umbrella hire available; price not found
cala-galdana.note: Half-moon cove with lifeguards and toilets. Paddle boats and water sports for hire. Length not confirmed.

la-baule-beach.access: Easy; seafront promenade and cycle path along the bay
la-baule-beach.parking: Not confirmed; reserved accessible spaces nearby
la-baule-beach.sunbeds: Beach clubs and striped beach huts; sunbed prices not found
la-baule-beach.note: About 9 km long between Pornichet and Le Pouliguen. Lifeguards on duty in July and August only.

camogli-beach.access: Easy; a few minutes on foot from Camogli-San Fruttuoso station, down steps to the beach
camogli-beach.parking: Very limited and many spaces reserved for residents; park elsewhere and take the train
camogli-beach.sunbeds: Paid lidos about 40 EUR/day for two sunbeds and an umbrella (spring figure); free stretch available
camogli-beach.food: Cafes and restaurants in the village and by the harbour
camogli-beach.note: Grey pebbles, some black sand. Free stretch has basic showers. Water shoes useful for kids.

bidart-beach.parking: Not confirmed for this beach; nearby Uhabia beach has free car parks
bidart-beach.sunbeds: Not confirmed; surf beach, bring own shade
bidart-beach.note: Lifeguards in peak season. Popular with surfers. Check the swell and flags before swimming.

playa-de-valdevaqueros.access: Dusty track signposted off the N-340
playa-de-valdevaqueros.parking: Small paid car parks; one guide says about 5 EUR/day, verify current fee
playa-de-valdevaqueros.sunbeds: None found; wind and kite beach, bring own shade
playa-de-valdevaqueros.food: Several chiringuitos; a burger stand open into the evening
playa-de-valdevaqueros.note: Kite area is the south end; north end suits swimmers and windsurfers. Rocks at the south end. Beach length reported 4 to 5 km.

costa-rei.access: Easy; road access along the beach
costa-rei.parking: Parking available near the beach establishments; details vary by stretch
costa-rei.sunbeds: Equipment hire at the paid establishments; price not found; free stretches alternate
costa-rei.note: Length reported 8 to 12 km depending on source. Fine white sand and shallow clear water.

sant-elm-beach.access: Easy; in the village of Sant Elm
sant-elm-beach.parking: Guarded paid car park at the village entrance; free parking further away
sant-elm-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and parasols reported seasonally; rental uncertain in recent years
sant-elm-beach.food: Cafes and restaurants in the village
sant-elm-beach.note: Boats to Sa Dragonera nature park leave from the port. Sa Trapa trail is about 9 km.

tamariu-beach.parking: Blue-zone street parking and staffed paid car parks; spaces scarce in summer
tamariu-beach.food: Bars and restaurants along the seafront; about ten in the village
tamariu-beach.note: Beach about 180 m long and 40 m wide. Showers, toilets and a summer lifeguard.

agios-gordios-beach.access: Easy; steps and path from the village
agios-gordios-beach.parking: Scarce in July and August; large municipal car park a little above the village
agios-gordios-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas for hire; some free with a restaurant order; price not found
agios-gordios-beach.note: About 1 km, Blue Flag reported. Sand at the south end, pebbles at the north. Pedal boats and canoes for hire.

alimini-beach.access: Easy; road access to beach bars and resort beaches
alimini-beach.parking: Limited and busy in summer; some free public parking reported
alimini-beach.sunbeds: Loungers at beach bars; one older review reported 10 EUR for two loungers and an umbrella
alimini-beach.note: Length not confirmed. Currents can shrink the beach and bring in volcanic sand.

marina-grande-beach.access: Moderate; steep lane and stairs down from the town; buses from Piazza Tasso
marina-grande-beach.sunbeds: None found at Marina Grande; paid sunbeds are at Marina Piccola
marina-grande-beach.food: Seafront restaurants and cafes at the harbour
marina-grande-beach.note: Rocky beach of volcanic sand; bring a mat or chair. Marina Piccola is reached by lift from the town.

praia-do-vale-do-lobo.access: Easy; path down from the resort Praca
praia-do-vale-do-lobo.parking: Plenty of paid parking; bring coins for the meter
praia-do-vale-do-lobo.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas; first rows reserved for resort guests; one visitor paid about 40 EUR
praia-do-vale-do-lobo.food: Restaurants and bars in the Praca area and beach bars
praia-do-vale-do-lobo.note: Blue Flag listing is undated, so confirm current status. Massage station on the beach.

kavourotrypes-beach.access: Easy; 3-4 minute walk from the car park along a path through the woods
kavourotrypes-beach.parking: Free parking above the beach; fills up quickly in summer
kavourotrypes-beach.sunbeds: A few sunbeds near the main cove; many nearby coves are completely natural
kavourotrypes-beach.food: Small beach bar near the main cove; reviews of the bar are mixed
kavourotrypes-beach.note: Toilet at the car park; no showers or cabins. Very crowded after 11 am in July and August.

super-paradise-beach.access: Easy by car; the last stretch of road is steep; local bus from Mykonos Town
super-paradise-beach.parking: Free parking; valet attendants may expect a tip of around 5 EUR for a full day
super-paradise-beach.sunbeds: Paid sunbeds at the clubs; guides report about 25-40 EUR for two with an umbrella; one 2022 review reported 120 EUR for two
super-paradise-beach.food: Jackie O and the Super Paradise club have bars and a self-service restaurant
super-paradise-beach.note: Prices vary widely by season, so check before you sit. Water sports and massages are offered on the sand.

agios-sostis-beach.access: Car or scooter only; the access road is narrow, with room for one lane of traffic in places
agios-sostis-beach.parking: Roadside parking near the beach; arrive early
agios-sostis-beach.sunbeds: None; no umbrellas to rent, so bring your own shade
agios-sostis-beach.food: Kiki taverna nearby, reported as expensive; bring cash
agios-sostis-beach.note: No bus or beach boat. Nude sunbathing area at the far end of the beach.

kalamitsi-beach.access: Challenging; steep, narrow road, and cars cannot pass in places; Megali Petra is reached on foot from Kavalikefta
kalamitsi-beach.parking: Small private parking at Kavalikefta; limited parking at Avali; arrive early
kalamitsi-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and parasols for rent at Kavalikefta; none at Megali Petra; limited sunbeds at Avali
kalamitsi-beach.food: Restaurant above Kavalikefta; snack bar above Avali serving lunch
kalamitsi-beach.note: Kavalikefta, Megali Petra and Avali are different beaches within a short distance of each other.

porto-timoni.access: Challenging; 30-40 minute walk each way from Afionas on a rocky, partly steep path
porto-timoni.parking: Limited parking in Afionas, fills fast in summer; one guide mentions a paid lot of about 5 EUR
porto-timoni.sunbeds: None reported; bring water and shade
porto-timoni.food: Taverna Anemos in Afionas has views over the twin bay
porto-timoni.note: A further trail leads from the beach to a quieter neighbouring bay. The bus to Afionas is slow and infrequent.

kolona-beach.access: Moderate; rough dirt road from Chora to the parking at Fikiada, or taxi boat from Merichas in about 15 minutes
kolona-beach.parking: Parking at Fikiada, not at the beach itself
kolona-beach.sunbeds: Sources conflict; a beach bar reportedly has some sunbeds and umbrellas, and most of the shore is unorganised
kolona-beach.food: A taverna or beach bar on part of the beach, reportedly with music
kolona-beach.note: Very little natural shade; only a couple of trees. Sunbed availability and prices vary, so check locally.

sa-colonia-beach.access: Easy; about 10 minutes on foot from the car park; bus stop Chia Tabacchi
sa-colonia-beach.parking: Paid in season, about 7-8 EUR a day (full-day tickets); free out of season; a cheaper rate after 4 pm is reported
sa-colonia-beach.sunbeds: Kiosks rent loungers, umbrellas and sun beds
sa-colonia-beach.food: Kiosks serve food and drinks; no large beach clubs
sa-colonia-beach.note: Clean toilets and changing rooms reported at the parking areas and kiosks; one reviewer paid 0.50 EUR. Check current prices.

fiascherino-beach.access: Easy; steps lead down to the sea
fiascherino-beach.parking: Paid parking about 200 m away (around 15 EUR reported); free parking about 500 m away
fiascherino-beach.sunbeds: Equipped stretch with deckchairs and umbrellas; one visitor paid 25 EUR for two sunbeds and an umbrella from 2 pm
fiascherino-beach.food: Beach club between Fiascherino and Lerici; check locally for other options
fiascherino-beach.note: Part of the beach is free. Prices and season dates are from older reviews, so confirm locally.

punta-prosciutto.access: Easy by car; use the established access paths through the dunes
punta-prosciutto.parking: Paid, seasonal parking; bring change; very busy in July and August
punta-prosciutto.sunbeds: Lidos rent loungers and umbrellas; one guide says about 80 percent of the beach is free, but a reviewer reports most sand taken by paid lidos
punta-prosciutto.food: Bars and snack bars at the lidos; Samana Beach has a bar, cafe and fast food
punta-prosciutto.note: The area is protected; stay on the paths and take your waste with you.

calamosche-beach.access: Moderate; walk of about 1 to 1.2 km from the car park, roughly 20 minutes
calamosche-beach.parking: Private car park about 5 EUR reported, plus reserve entry of about 3.5 to 5 EUR
calamosche-beach.sunbeds: None; no shade, so bring an umbrella
calamosche-beach.food: A bar and showers are reported at the car park
calamosche-beach.note: The reserve reportedly limits visits to about 550 people a day. I found no booking system or opening hours, so check with the Vendicari reserve.

praia-do-zavial.access: Easy; leave the N125 near Raposeira and follow the signs
praia-do-zavial.parking: Car park near the restaurant; limited in summer, so arrive early
praia-do-zavial.sunbeds: Sources disagree; some report sunbeds, one blog describes no neat rows of loungers or parasols
praia-do-zavial.food: Restaurante Zavial behind the beach serves fresh fish and chicken piri-piri; reportedly open in high season only and cash only
praia-do-zavial.note: Toilets but no showers. Lifeguards in peak season.

praia-da-ingrina.parking: Car park close to the beach
praia-da-ingrina.food: Beach restaurant specialising in fresh fish and seafood, with a bar
praia-da-ingrina.note: Toilets and summer lifeguards. One source says there is no shade. Restaurant hours and rental availability may have changed.

praia-da-salema.access: Easy; steps and a walkway lead down from the village
praia-da-salema.parking: Parking near the village; fills up at weekends and in peak season
praia-da-salema.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas near the restaurants; the eastern end is quieter with no rentals
praia-da-salema.food: Several restaurants along the beach, including Olhos n Agua and O Lourenco
praia-da-salema.note: Blue Flag status is cited by several sources; confirm the current season.

playa-de-los-lances.access: Easy by car or from Tarifa bus station
playa-de-los-lances.parking: Plenty of parking for private cars
playa-de-los-lances.sunbeds: Sunbeds reported at Lances Sur; strong wind makes sunbathing unpleasant
playa-de-los-lances.food: Beach bars and hotel restaurants nearby, such as Waves Beach Bar and Chiringuito Arte Vida
playa-de-los-lances.note: Wind is the main factor: poniente and levante both blow, and levante is offshore. Kiting rules in summer are unconfirmed, so check locally.

cala-torta.access: Moderate; 15-30 minute walk each way on an unmarked, uneven trail with an uphill return
cala-torta.parking: Unpaved roadside parking about 1.2-1.5 km from the beach; driving further is not allowed
cala-torta.sunbeds: None; no lifeguards, so bring water and shade
cala-torta.food: A small food truck or restaurant just before the trail starts
cala-torta.note: Not suitable for wheelchairs or strollers. Northerly winds can cause undercurrents, and mobile signal is reported as poor.

playa-de-calblanque.access: Moderate; summer car access is largely restricted, so use the bus, walk in, or ask at the visitor centre
playa-de-calblanque.parking: A free lot of about 30 spaces is reported near the coves, possibly closed in high season (2021 comment)
playa-de-calblanque.food: I found no chiringuito; bring food and water
playa-de-calblanque.note: Las Cobaticas visitor centre is inside the park. A shuttle bus is mentioned for busy periods. Confirm current summer rules with the regional park.

stara-baska-beach.access: Easy to moderate; sources disagree on road versus sea access to the main beach
stara-baska-beach.parking: Limited roadside parking; several beaches before the village entrance are reached on foot
stara-baska-beach.sunbeds: One guide lists beach chairs and umbrellas; I found no rental details
stara-baska-beach.food: A beach bar and restaurants listed; Restoran Cicibela near Pe En Bay
stara-baska-beach.note: Oprna cove has a small bar in peak season, no showers, and a steep 10-15 minute walk from limited parking.

kupari-beach.access: Easy by road from Dubrovnik, about 10 km; check for fencing around the old hotels
kupari-beach.parking: No parking details found; check on arrival
kupari-beach.sunbeds: None found; the old bathing facilities have been disused for years
kupari-beach.note: Redevelopment works began in 2025 and conditions may have changed since. The pebble shore is still visited.

zavala-beach.access: Moderate; road from Pitve through a tunnel
zavala-beach.parking: Signposted car park near the beach
zavala-beach.food: Konoba Zavala, Zaca Bar and Restaurant, Restaurant Davor; bars Terra Nova and Zavala Port Beach
zavala-beach.note: The shore is mostly pebbles, gravel and concrete slabs with some rocks, and it suits families.

nin-beach.access: Easy; walk from the parking area through the pines
nin-beach.parking: Public parking in the pine forest; paid in summer, free in September
nin-beach.sunbeds: Sun loungers and umbrellas for rent
nin-beach.food: A beach bar near the public parking
nin-beach.note: Shallow for about 500 m, which suits young children. The lagoon shifts with wind and weather; the mud is called peloid.

pakostane-beach.access: Easy; the beach sits at the edge of the village in a pine forest
pakostane-beach.parking: Car park among the trees at the entrance; one listing says free parking
pakostane-beach.sunbeds: Plenty of sun loungers reported at the resort beach
pakostane-beach.food: Resort facilities; check for public options in the village
pakostane-beach.note: Shoreline is described as sand, shingle and rocky terraces. Soline is a separate beach nearby.

plage-de-piemanson.parking: Public car park open 6:00 to 22:00 per the Arles tourist office
plage-de-piemanson.note: Sources conflict on camping: one reports a tolerance from 1 May to 30 September, another says camping is banned on the beach. Check with Arles. East end is naturist.

plage-de-tahiti.access: Easy by road; free public access to the beach
plage-de-tahiti.parking: Paid in summer; Pampelonne parking reported free before 11 am and after 5 pm in season
plage-de-tahiti.sunbeds: Paid sunbeds at the clubs; one Pampelonne listing shows 40-60 EUR per sunbed and parasols at 8 EUR
plage-de-tahiti.food: Restaurant Tahiti Beach and Tiki Club among the beach restaurants; lunch prices are high
plage-de-tahiti.note: Opening dates and prices are for earlier seasons; confirm directly with the clubs.

plage-de-la-palue.access: Moderate; follow signs to Morgat and Cap de la Chevre, through La Palue hamlet to the dune-top car park
plage-de-la-palue.parking: Large car park at the top of the dune; a 2021 order restricted some Crozon car parks, so check current rules
plage-de-la-palue.note: Swimming is reported as prohibited due to dangerous currents. At high tide a large part of the beach is covered. Crowded on weekends and holidays.

pointe-de-la-torche.access: Easy; park and walk to the point; the direct road can be closed to general traffic
pointe-de-la-torche.parking: Large car park and toilets (Brittany tourism); one local guide cites several lots and a 2 EUR shuttle, which may apply to events
pointe-de-la-torche.sunbeds: None; this is a surf beach
pointe-de-la-torche.food: Restaurants and surf shops nearby; none named in my sources
pointe-de-la-torche.note: Twenty Nine surf school is on the beach. Lifeguards only in July and August (1.30 pm to 7.30 pm). Waves are big and suit surfers with a good level.

mikri-vigla-beach.access: Drive or bus along the coast road from Naxos Town (about 20 km); the beach is flat and easy to reach from the roadside.
mikri-vigla-beach.parking: Free parking along the coastal road and on dirt areas behind the dunes.
mikri-vigla-beach.sunbeds: Few or none; this is mainly a kite and windsurf beach, so bring your own shade.
mikri-vigla-beach.food: A few tavernas and snack spots near the beach, plus the surf school cafes.
mikri-vigla-beach.note: Windy in the afternoon in summer, which suits kiters; mornings are calmer for swimming. Three surf schools operate here.

apella-beach.access: About 20 km (40 minutes) from Pigadia; the road ends at a car park above the cove, then a short path leads down. A public bus runs a few days a week, and excursion boats leave from Pigadia.
apella-beach.parking: A small car park by the taverna where the road ends.
apella-beach.sunbeds: Sunbed and umbrella sets are rented at the taverna (reported around 20 EUR per set).
apella-beach.food: A small taverna above the beach; bring extra water.
apella-beach.note: Pebble cove with very clear water. Check bus times in advance.

katergo-beach.access: Small boat from Karavostasi (about 10 minutes; about 12 to 14 EUR return reported), or hike 30 minutes from Livadi or about 50 minutes from the port.
katergo-beach.parking: No parking at the beach; park at Livadi or Karavostasi.
katergo-beach.sunbeds: None. There is almost no shade, so bring an umbrella.
katergo-beach.note: A wild cove with no facilities; go early and carry water.

kalafatis-beach.access: 11 to 12 km from Mykonos Town; bus from the Old Port or drive.
kalafatis-beach.parking: Free street parking near the beach.
kalafatis-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas on the organised section (about 50 EUR for an umbrella and two sunbeds reported).
kalafatis-beach.food: Around three restaurants and bars along the beach.
kalafatis-beach.note: Windsurf and kitesurf schools operate here; the eastern end is wilder and quieter.

agios-ioannis-beach.access: Reached by road from Zagora and the Pelion mountain roads; the beach sits right by the village.
agios-ioannis-beach.parking: Free parking is hard to find in summer; some hotels have small private lots, sometimes for a fee.
agios-ioannis-beach.sunbeds: Limited information; a few spots may rent loungers in season.
agios-ioannis-beach.food: Several tavernas along the boardwalk by the beach.
agios-ioannis-beach.note: Pebble beach; water shoes help. Arrive early in July and August.

la-cinta-beach.access: About 2 km from San Teodoro; road access, with bus service in summer.
la-cinta-beach.parking: Free parking in places and paid lots near the entrances (hourly rates, pricey in peak season).
la-cinta-beach.sunbeds: Beach clubs rent sunbeds and umbrellas (about 40 to 70 EUR reported in high season).
la-cinta-beach.food: Beach bars and restaurants along the beach.
la-cinta-beach.note: A quieter stretch lies 10 to 15 minutes along the sand from the main entrance.

torre-guaceto-beach.access: From the reserve entrance, a flat path of about 1.4 km or a shuttle to the beach.
torre-guaceto-beach.parking: Paid parking at the entrance (about 4 to 8 EUR per day, including the shuttle).
torre-guaceto-beach.sunbeds: No sunbed rental on most of the beach; bring your own shade.
torre-guaceto-beach.food: A small bar and toilets near the entrance; bring water.
torre-guaceto-beach.note: Marine reserve with controlled access; the shuttle can wait around 20 minutes in high season.

marina-di-praia.access: A steep road and stairs down from the Amalfi Coast road; the SITA bus stops nearby.
marina-di-praia.parking: Roadside parking above and a private summer car park.
marina-di-praia.sunbeds: Limited; a beach club operates in season (rental details unverified).
marina-di-praia.food: A few restaurants at the cove, including Il Pirata.
marina-di-praia.note: Steep stairs back up; the cove gets shade early in the afternoon.

scilla-marina-grande.access: Directly in the town of Scilla, a short walk from the station and old quarter.
scilla-marina-grande.parking: A car park near the beach (reported about 2 EUR per hour) and street parking.
scilla-marina-grande.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas rented by beach bars.
scilla-marina-grande.food: Four beach bars and several restaurants nearby.
scilla-marina-grande.note: Chianalea is uphill from the beach; allow extra time for the walk.

fornillo-beach.access: About 10 minutes on foot from Spiaggia Grande with long stairs, or by sea shuttle.
fornillo-beach.parking: No beach parking; use town car parks.
fornillo-beach.sunbeds: Lidos rent sunbeds and umbrellas (about 35 EUR per person at one club reported).
fornillo-beach.food: Seafood restaurants on the beach, including Da Ferdinando.
fornillo-beach.note: Calmer and less crowded than the main beach; stairs make it unsuitable for mobility problems.

playa-de-torimbia.access: On foot only, about 1 km from the top car park; 15 to 20 minutes down and 20 to 25 minutes back up.
playa-de-torimbia.parking: A small free car park at the top, with roadside parking when full.
playa-de-torimbia.note: Clothes-optional; lifeguards and showers in summer.

praia-da-lanzada.access: By road from Sanxenxo and O Grove; flat access across the dunes.
praia-da-lanzada.sunbeds: No regular rental; bring your own shade.
praia-da-lanzada.food: Chiringuitos and restaurants nearby, such as Pragueira Beach.
praia-da-lanzada.note: Big waves and cold water; swim only where lifeguards allow.

cala-deia.access: Narrow, winding road from Deia village down to the cove; a bus or taxi is easier than driving.
cala-deia.parking: Very limited; a larger car park with about 60 extra spaces has been planned.
cala-deia.food: Two restaurants by the cove: Ca s Patro March (seasonal) and Ca n Lluc.
cala-deia.note: Pebble cove that fills quickly; go early. Anchoring is not advisable.

playa-de-berria.access: 2.5 km north of Santona; bus or short drive, flat access.
playa-de-berria.note: Lifeguards in summer; best at low tide when more sand is exposed.

cala-santanyi.access: A short walk from the public car park down to the cove.
cala-santanyi.parking: A free public car park a short walk away; it fills early.
cala-santanyi.sunbeds: Parasols and sunbeds can be rented.
cala-santanyi.food: Restaurants such as Voramar near the beach.
cala-santanyi.note: Break-ins are reported, so leave nothing in the car. Es Pontas arch is reached by a coastal path.

praia-de-sao-rafael.access: Stairs down the cliff from the car park and streets above.
praia-de-sao-rafael.parking: Limited in summer and restricted; arrive early.
praia-de-sao-rafael.sunbeds: Sunbeds on the left section of the beach.
praia-de-sao-rafael.note: Free toilets and showers; Blue Flag status cited in recent years.

praia-do-evaristo.access: Wooden boardwalks from the central car park to the sand.
praia-do-evaristo.sunbeds: Loungers and parasols; pedalos for hire.
praia-do-evaristo.food: The original restaurant was lost to a fire in October 2023; a temporary canteen has been reported, so check ahead.
praia-do-evaristo.note: Lifeguards in summer; showers and toilets at the east end. Natural rock pool at low tide.

porto-santo-beach.access: Along the island: the beach is long and flat; the ferry from Madeira runs daily.
porto-santo-beach.parking: Near the main access points; Pestana section free parking not verified.
porto-santo-beach.sunbeds: Sunbed concession at the main sections.
porto-santo-beach.food: A restaurant and bars on the Fontinha section.
porto-santo-beach.note: Fontinha (720 m) has changing rooms and Blue Flag status; the beach runs about 9 km.

praia-de-santa-barbara.access: Near Ribeira Grande on the north coast of Sao Miguel; by road.
praia-de-santa-barbara.food: Bars on site; the restaurant has been under renovation.
praia-de-santa-barbara.note: Lifeguards, toilets, showers and a surf school. Strong currents.

kasjuni-beach.access: About 3 km from the old town; city bus 12 or a coastal walk.
kasjuni-beach.parking: A managed car park that fills fast; arrive early.
kasjuni-beach.food: Joe Beach Lounge and a bar.
kasjuni-beach.note: Pebble beach under Marjan hill; clear water.

sveti-jakov-beach.access: About 150 steps down from the Sveti Jakov church; buses 5 and 8 run along the main road above.
sveti-jakov-beach.parking: Limited near the church; prices and spaces vary.
sveti-jakov-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas for rent (about 15 EUR each reported).
sveti-jakov-beach.food: A beach bar and restaurant, with toilets and showers; may close after mid-October.
sveti-jakov-beach.note: Not suitable for people with mobility problems.

plage-de-roccapina.access: A rough dirt track of about 2.5 km from the main road; potholes.
plage-de-roccapina.parking: A free dirt car park at the end of the track; it fills quickly.
plage-de-roccapina.food: None on site; nearest at the Roccapina hamlet and Col de Curali.
plage-de-roccapina.note: A signposted walk from the main road is possible. Bring food, water and shade.

plage-de-la-cote-des-basques.access: Down stairs from the clifftop, or along the beach from the old port.
plage-de-la-cote-des-basques.parking: Limited nearby; town car parks are better.
plage-de-la-cote-des-basques.food: Cafes at the top of the cliff.
plage-de-la-cote-des-basques.note: The beach is covered at high tide; check tide times. Lifeguards April to October.

plage-des-grands-sables.access: Ferry from Lorient to Groix (about 45 minutes); then a short ride or walk to the beach.
plage-des-grands-sables.parking: A car park beside the beach.
plage-des-grands-sables.food: Nothing on the beach itself; bring food.
plage-des-grands-sables.note: Convex beach shaped by opposing currents; supervised in July and August.

omaha-beach.access: Drive to the beach; the direct path from the American cemetery is closed.
omaha-beach.parking: Free or paid depending on area and season; plenty at Saint-Laurent-sur-Mer.
omaha-beach.food: Cafes and shops in the villages nearby.
omaha-beach.note: Swimming is allowed; check tide times. Visit with respect, since this is a memorial site.

gidaki-beach.access: Small boats run from Vathy in summer, or walk a rough footpath of roughly 25 minutes from Skinos and up to an hour from Vathy.
gidaki-beach.parking: No road to the beach and no parking; park in the villages and walk, or take a boat.
gidaki-beach.sunbeds: A limited number of sunbeds, around 30 reported, near the snack bar in season.
gidaki-beach.food: A seasonal canteen or snack bar; sources disagree on what is open, so bring your own water and food.
gidaki-beach.note: Pebbles and cliffs; take shoes for the path. Boat trips from Vathy can be pricey, so compare operators.

dafnoudi-beach.access: A rocky trail through pine forest of about 600 m and roughly 10 minutes; sturdy shoes advised and it is steeper on the way back up.
dafnoudi-beach.parking: Free parking at the trailhead, reported to have plenty of space.
dafnoudi-beach.sunbeds: No sunbeds or umbrellas reported; bring your own shade.
dafnoudi-beach.food: No facilities on the beach; Fiskardo, a few minutes by car, has tavernas and shops.
dafnoudi-beach.note: Small pebble beach with clear water; best on calm days. Take water, and watch your step on the path.

kalamaki-beach.access: Walk down from the village or the road above; the beach is flat and easy.
kalamaki-beach.parking: No authoritative information on parking; spaces near the village are generally available.
kalamaki-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas are permitted in limited numbers and are meant to be cleared at night.
kalamaki-beach.food: A small canteen on the sand and a taverna above that sends drinks down by pulley; more places in the village.
kalamaki-beach.note: Protected nesting beach: public access is restricted from sunset to sunrise, do not disturb nest markers, and motorised water sports are banned.

mylos-beach.access: A rough, uneven path through forest of about 1 km, 15-30 minutes depending on pace; sturdy shoes needed. A taxi boat also runs from Agios Nikitas (reported about 6 EUR each way).
mylos-beach.parking: No parking at the beach; use the car parks in Agios Nikitas.
mylos-beach.sunbeds: One bar rents sunbeds and umbrellas; the beach is otherwise unorganised.
mylos-beach.food: One bar only; bring water and snacks.
mylos-beach.note: Little shade and no other facilities. Rental prices are reported to be high, so bring your own gear if you can.

sansone-beach.access: A steep path of about 10 minutes on foot, starting shortly before the Viticcio turning; not suitable for wheelchairs or strollers.
sansone-beach.parking: Free parking is limited and fills early, street parking is fined, and a small paid lot costs around 18 EUR a day.
sansone-beach.sunbeds: Umbrella and sunbeds can be rented; one visitor paid about 40 EUR for the day, so check prices first.
sansone-beach.food: A beach bar rents umbrellas; bring lunch for a full day.
sansone-beach.note: White pebbles make the water look vivid but rough underfoot; very busy in July and August.

fetovaia-beach.access: Short walk from the car park at the back of the beach; flat and easy.
fetovaia-beach.parking: A car park with a small number of free spaces plus paid spots; fills early. Alternative: park in Marina di Campo, about 10 km away, and take the bus.
fetovaia-beach.sunbeds: Beach clubs rent sunbeds and umbrellas; there are also free sections to lay a towel.
fetovaia-beach.food: Beach bars and restaurants along the shore; more in the village above.
fetovaia-beach.note: Often very crowded in high season. No camper-specific information found, so check local signs and Campo nell Elba rules.

cala-sinzias.access: Walk straight onto the sand from the road; shallow, gentle entry.
cala-sinzias.parking: Parking around the approach road and the nearby resort; can be tight in August.
cala-sinzias.sunbeds: Sunbeds and umbrellas available, including those run by the nearby resort.
cala-sinzias.food: A beach bar and restaurants nearby; the resort also has a restaurant.
cala-sinzias.note: Shallow water makes it good for small children. No official lifeguard or price details found, so ask locally.

torre-dell-orso-beach.access: Walk from the town streets directly onto the sand; flat and easy.
torre-dell-orso-beach.parking: No reliable public figures found; expect busy car parks in July and August.
torre-dell-orso-beach.sunbeds: Lidos rent two loungers and an umbrella, reported around 20-35 EUR in June and 35-50 EUR or more in August; free beach space exists too.
torre-dell-orso-beach.food: Beach bars and restaurants along the front.
torre-dell-orso-beach.note: The free beach fills quickly; weekdays are calmer than weekends. Bring your own umbrella and towel to avoid fees.

budoni-beach.access: Direct access from the car park through the dunes; flat and easy.
budoni-beach.parking: A large pay car park; reported around 3 EUR a day or 0.50 EUR an hour in shoulder season.
budoni-beach.sunbeds: Sunbeds, umbrellas and dinghy rental in equipped sections; other areas are free.
budoni-beach.food: Beach bars and restaurants; showers available.
budoni-beach.note: A September visitor reported seaweed in the southern third, so conditions vary; shallow, sloping water suits families.

playa-de-las-catedrales.access: A staircase leads down to the sand, and the caves can be explored only around low tide. Permits are needed in high season.
playa-de-las-catedrales.parking: Two large free car parks; the paved one fills fast, the second is a gravel meadow.
playa-de-las-catedrales.sunbeds: No sunbeds; this is a natural monument, not a beach resort.
playa-de-las-catedrales.food: No food on the beach; bars and restaurants in Ribadeo and Rinlo.
playa-de-las-catedrales.note: Visiting is by free online permit up to 30 days ahead for up to 25 people in busy periods (Easter, summer, holiday weekends); check the official booking site.

playa-de-ris.access: Direct access from the promenade and streets; flat and easy.
playa-de-ris.parking: Parking near the beach; it fills quickly in July and August, so arrive early in the morning.
playa-de-ris.sunbeds: Some rental of sunbeds and mats reported; confirm in season.
playa-de-ris.food: Restaurants and bars nearby; sources disagree on whether a beach bar sits right on the sand.
playa-de-ris.note: Lifeguards on duty in summer. Camping Playa de Ris sits behind the beach.

cala-d-hort.access: A 10-minute walk from the main car park to the sand; flat road and easy steps.
cala-d-hort.parking: An unpaved car park for about 200 vehicles beside the access road, free in 2025 with fees expected from 2026; arrive early.
cala-d-hort.sunbeds: Sunbeds, daybeds and parasols for rent.
cala-d-hort.food: Three beachside restaurants focused on fish and seafood, including Es Boldado known for paella; a bar on the beach.
cala-d-hort.note: Blue Flag for many years and lifeguarded; the beach is small (about 150 m) and very busy in summer.

playa-de-el-puntal.access: Easy access by road with a promenade overlooking Rodiles and Misiego.
playa-de-el-puntal.parking: Parking near the beach; it can fill up in high season.
playa-de-el-puntal.sunbeds: No sunbed rental reported; bring your own shade.
playa-de-el-puntal.food: Cafes and restaurants in the nearby village and the estuary area.
playa-de-el-puntal.note: Showers and a rescue service are listed by the Asturias tourism board; pets are banned from 1 June to 30 September.

playa-de-bolnuevo.access: Walk onto the beach from the promenade or the Gredas car park; flat and easy.
playa-de-bolnuevo.parking: Large open car park near the Gredas, rarely full even in summer; street parking in town is tight. Camper rules vary and some user reports mention time limits.
playa-de-bolnuevo.food: Bars and restaurants along the beach front.
playa-de-bolnuevo.note: The main beach is about 1.6 km long. Do not climb on the eroded rock formations.

praia-da-foz-do-arelho.access: Walk straight onto the sand from the village and promenade; easy.
praia-da-foz-do-arelho.parking: Free and paid options nearby; lots fill in peak season, though overflow areas are available.
praia-da-foz-do-arelho.sunbeds: No sunbed rental confirmed; beach clubs may offer seating, so ask on arrival.
praia-da-foz-do-arelho.food: Cais da Praia on the sand (live music and rooftop seating), Cabana do Pescador for seafood, Cocos Beach Club for pizza and cocktails.
praia-da-foz-do-arelho.note: Lagoon and ocean sides differ; water sports on the lagoon. No lifeguard details found, so check flags.

praia-dos-tres-irmaos.access: A staircase of many steps leads down; lifts at nearby holiday complexes.
praia-dos-tres-irmaos.parking: Parking nearby with disabled bays; arrive early in peak season.
praia-dos-tres-irmaos.food: Nearby restaurants such as Canico; toilets beneath some of them.
praia-dos-tres-irmaos.note: Cave routes depend on the tide; check times before you explore.

praia-da-ilha-do-pessegueiro.access: Paved access road to a large car park, then a short walk to the sand.
praia-da-ilha-do-pessegueiro.parking: A paved municipal access road and space for about 131 vehicles.
praia-da-ilha-do-pessegueiro.sunbeds: No sunbed rental confirmed; bring your own umbrella.
praia-da-ilha-do-pessegueiro.food: Several restaurants, including A Ilha facing the island, serving grilled fish; reservations suggested.
praia-da-ilha-do-pessegueiro.note: Part of a protected natural park; showers and toilets reported.
